# LibreCV

> LibreCV is a free CV and motivation-letter builder. The only public site is https://librecv.org/. There is no GitHub Pages site. There is no account. The document stays in the browser. The project's own code is CC0-1.0, as close to the public domain as the law here allows. It is not the LibreCV computer-vision association, and it is not the SimpleCV Python library.

LibreCV is a visual editor. You design a page with blocks. It is not a markdown file, and it does not ask you to create an account.

## What it does

- [Open LibreCV](https://librecv.org/): build a CV or a motivation letter in the browser
- A step-by-step guide, a blank page, pasted text, demo data, or an AI template
- Pasted text uses Chrome's on-device model. Another browser warns first. Sorting text into blocks still works without that model
- The AI template is copied on this device. The text is not sent to a LibreCV server. The template keeps a photo frame in the sidebar, with its shape, and leaves the picture file out. An https address on that frame can load the picture
- Use your own AI is a button in the editor's top bar. Get text copies a template. The person pastes that into their own AI. An old CV and the job are optional. The answer should be one code block. Paste text puts it back on the page
- Download a PDF whose text can be selected. That PDF can be opened in the editor again. Saves, in the header, keeps more than one CV or letter in this browser. Reset clears them. Nothing is uploaded
- The interface is in English and Dutch. A new visit starts in English. `?lang=nl` opens it in Dutch
- [Dutch introduction](https://librecv.org/nl/)
- [Motivation letter](https://librecv.org/motivation-letter/) and [Motivatiebrief](https://librecv.org/nl/motivatiebrief/)
- [CV examples](https://librecv.org/templates/), including a software engineer CV and letter and a registered nurse CV and letter, in English and Dutch. Each example opens in the editor. The names are invented
- [PDF command](https://librecv.org/cli/) and [het Nederlandse commando](https://librecv.org/nl/cli/): `npm run pdf -- catalog/software-engineer-cv.txt -o cv.pdf` writes a selectable-text PDF from the same block. An id such as `software-engineer-cv` works too. `--lang nl` sets the Dutch headings. The PDF carries document.json. The command-line PDF uses a standard typeface and paints the sidebar colour, the photo mark, the labels and the skill chips. The download in the editor uses the typeface on the page
- The names on the example pages are invented
- Feedback is optional. The button is in the editor header and in the footer of each setup step. Private notes: https://librecv.org/feedback/ . Instructions for an assistant: https://librecv.org/feedback.txt . A public GitHub issue uses https://github.com/Vabian124/LibreCV/issues/new?template=feedback.yml and must not include a CV or letter

## What it does not do

- No account and no login. The document is not uploaded. A feedback note includes the text only when that box is ticked
- It does not add a watermark
- It does not claim a search ranking
- The libraries keep their own licenses. See NOTICE in the repository

## Code

- [Source code](https://github.com/Vabian124/LibreCV): public repository, branch master. The site is only https://librecv.org/. There is no GitHub Pages site
- License: https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/
